messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate in region-us-west-2. Error class: model-runner 5xx (segfault/OOM) — SLO impact: increased tail latency and failed requests. Root thread: 1824000123
ryan: I'm on it, paging runtime team. Paging @alex @maria @sam — please join.
alex: on my way, pulling logs now. any customer reports?
support-bot: Customer-facing ticket created: INC-2026-458 — multiple customers reporting intermittent 502s, some timeouts.
maria: seeing spikes on the model-runner-3 deployment. /metrics shows OOM kills on a subset of replicas.
sam: interesting — recent deploy yesterday to change KV cache behavior? did we roll a new model binary?
ryan: yes, deploy-bot shows a canary push of runtime v2.14 at 02:10 UTC yesterday to 10% then 100% at 03:05.
alex: grabbing pod logs now.
eng-runtime: paste: `kubectl -n inference logs model-runner-3-5f6d8 -c runner --since=10m` output:
```
[2026-03-14T10:47:21Z] INFO: init kv cache
[2026-03-14T10:47:34Z] WARNING: GPU memory pressure: 93% used
[2026-03-14T10:47:38Z] ERROR: runtime segfault at 0x7ff... backtrace: ...
[2026-03-14T10:47:38Z] CRITICAL: process killed by signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
[2026-03-14T10:47:39Z] kubernetes: liveness probe failed
```
alex: pattern: segfault in C++ attention kernel during kv-cache warmup for long-context requests. Same stacktrace across several pods.
maria: I'm seeing OOM kills on different hosts too when sequence length spikes above 4096. Looks like kernel regression.
ryan: mitigation plan (short): 1) remove heavy long-context traffic by applying a routing rule to fallback smaller-context model; 2) scale down replica concurrency and disable batching on runner-3; 3) restart affected pods; 4) if unstable, rollback runtime to v2.13.
sam: I can flip routing quickly. Which fallback model id? smallest drop in quality but stable?
carla: use model-redwood-small-4096 as fallback; it has been validated for these customers.
jason: I'll disable batching and reduce max_concurrency from 8 -> 2 on runner-3 via k8s configmap patch. command: `kubectl -n inference patch cm runner-config --patch '{"data":{"max_concurrency":"2","enable_batching":"false"}}'`
alex: applying that now.
eng-runtime: applied patch, restarting pods controlled rollout.
eng-runtime: restart commands:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/model-runner-3
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-runner-3 -w
```
ryan: routing change in progress: updating smart-router policy to divert traffic with sequence_length > 2048 to model-redwood-small-4096.
sam: updated router policy, will monitor.
carla: posting status to customers: "We are mitigating elevated 5xx errors by temporarily routing long-context requests to a stable model variant and restarting affected inference workers. Some requests may see decreased max-length support; no data loss expected."
support-bot: Customer notification sent to impacted customers via status page update.
alex: after restart, pods come up but one pod still OOMs at 10:58:12Z. Logs show a fast memcpy in new attention kernel:
```
[2026-03-14T10:58:12Z] ERROR: cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory
[2026-03-14T10:58:12Z] CRITICAL: aborting process
```
maria: that suggests a memory accounting bug when the kernel path is hit; fallback routing should reduce frequency but code fix needed.
ryan: do we have a quick rollback option to v2.13? what's the risk?
eng-runtime: rollback is available. v2.13 image tagged and in registry. Rolling back will trigger graceful reconnects and minor latency bump.
sam: recommend rollback. we still see residual 502s after routing change.
carla: agree, rollback to restore stability ASAP. I'll coordinate with deploy-bot.
eng-runtime: initiating rollback to v2.13 now: `deploy-bot: rolling back runtime/model-runner to v2.13 (image: registry.redwood/inference/runner:v2.13)`
incident-bot: NOTE: Rolling back runtime may trigger short-term request failures during reconnects. Autoscaler is active.
jason: scaling replicas down to 3 temporarily to avoid hitting hot nodes: `kubectl -n inference scale deploy/model-runner-3 --replicas=3`
eng-runtime: rollback finished at 11:07:02Z. Health checks passing.
ryan: monitoring metrics: 5xx rate dropping. Observability dashboard: error rate returned to baseline 3m after rollback.
support-bot: update: customers notified that issue is mitigated; support ticket set to monitoring.
maria: tagging suspicious commit in attention-kernel PR: `a7f4c3b` which introduced a memcopy optimization. Opening hotfix PR to revert kernel change.
alex: capturing logs and core dumps for postmortem. uploading to S3: s3://incidents/1824000123/core-dumps/*.
carla: handoff plan: Ryan will rotate off at 12:00 UTC; @maria will take oncall for the next shift and continue kernel revert + validation.
ryan: handoff notes: mitigation performed = routing + disable batching + rollback to v2.13; customer impact = elevated 502/504 for ~40 minutes for a subset of customers; next steps = kernel revert PR, run long-context stress test, prepare canary with test harness.
maria: ack; I'll run extended stress tests and schedule a safe canary once PR is merged.
sam: please start a postmortem doc at: https://docs.redwood/internals/incidents/INC-2026-458-postmortem (will add timeline and RCA).
carla: thumbs: :thumbsup: Great coordination. We should also add an alert for sudden sequence_length distribution shifts.
jason: created alert: seq-length-spike in router; threshold 95th > 2048 -> page runtime team.
ryan: thanks everyone. handing off to @maria now. I'll stay reachable for 30m.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-458 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned to maria for follow-up.
maria: taking over. continuing with kernel revert and validation. I'll ping this thread with the postmortem link when ready.
eng-runtime: FYI we captured a sanitized core and reproducer; attaching to the PR for easier testing.
carla: closing communication loop with ops and support. If anything regresses, re-open this thread.
support-bot: Incident ticket updated: status = monitoring, owner = maria, customers notified.
maria: (final) postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood/internals/incidents/INC-2026-458-postmortem-draft — includes timeline, root cause (attention kernel memcpy regression), mitigation steps, and action items (revert, add tests, add alert).
ryan: thanks team, nice quick actions.
carla: :heart:
